project.name: Danube Forum Hotel
project.description: A fictional hotel construction project in Vienna with 120 guest rooms across six upper floors, plus reception, restaurant and conference facilities on the ground floor. The connected building has a 60 m by 24 m footprint, a western stair and lift core, and a central corridor on each guest floor. The imported programme includes wall layout, internal wall frames, electrical and plumbing installation, inspection, wall closure, deliveries, crane work and handover. A simulated layout robot marks wall positions only after a start check; a simulated survey drone compares measurements with the current drawing. Aurora connects site email and Telegram updates to these drawings and tasks. Dimensions and dates are synthetic planning assumptions.

tasks.name: Lift roof materials with mobile crane

assumptions: Fictional project for a product demonstration, not an approved construction design.
120 guest rooms, 20 per upper floor, with a connected ground floor and six upper floors.
Source geometry is preserved from the previous DeepSeek-generated hotel. Footprint 60 by 24 m; wall height 3 m; 10,080 square metres gross floor area.
All dates, durations, team assignments and delivery quantities are synthetic planning assumptions.
The layout robot is simulated. The canonical task name Frame partitions refers to marking wall positions on the floor, not assembling walls.
The survey drone is simulated. It reports measured fields and cannot approve work or change the programme.
Inspection tasks are planned appointments, never proof that an inspection passed.
H-100 revision A is the complete building. H-101 revision A is the first-floor detail. Revision B is supplied separately for the live email step.
No crew email addresses are inferred. Only explicitly configured demo channels may receive messages.
